factualBoundaries: 17.01 debut is 8 August 2017, as stated in the original brand announcement. Initial plan was 150 per dial colour.
The 19.01 has flared lugs, curved quick-release bars and 20mm replaceable straps. The brand is not described as universally lugless or equipped with integrated bracelets.
The 19.01 separates top crystal, gradient sapphire dial, lower crystal and titanium caseband. MSE100.1 is credited to Schwarz Etienne, not called a MING-made movement.
HyCeram and Polar White are distinct luminous materials, separate from the sapphire substrate. Not all MING luminous elements are called HyCeram.
The 37.05 Series 2 Special Edition uses 288.M1, approximately 38h reserve, 38mm diameter and 11.9mm thickness.
37.02 Minimalist uses SW300.M1 with approximately 45h reserve. Bluefin uses SW300.M1 with approximately 50h and a running seconds hand. These two factory figures are not silently harmonised.
CHF 3500 for the Minimalist is the maker's announced price effective 1 April 2026, sourced to the December 2025 letter. No live availability or checkout total is promised.
Bluefin's entire timing dial rotates using its second crown; fixed hour markers remain on the upper crystal. 600m is the manufacturer's stated rating, not the author's dive test.
The 2024 GPHG Sports Watch Prize is independently checked against the official prize list.
20.01 Series 5 uses a laser-machined titanium dial, not the sapphire FemtoMosaic process of other series. Its calibre 6361.M1 is credited to Agenhor.
Comet's fifth-generation case has triple-step lugs. 330.M2, 40mm, 10.33mm and approximately 50h are from the exact strap variant's specification.
Comet's DST adjustment is a manual two-position mechanism, not an automatic database of different national clock-change dates. The practical limitation is editorial inference from that construction.
Swiss-facility history in 2024 and current Malaysian/Swiss responsibilities are distinguished. No unsourced legal interpretation of Swiss Made regulations is included.
